kings1.2.p1.b1.text: As the time drew near for David to die, he charged his son Solomon,

kings1.2.p1.b2.text: “I am about to go the way of all the earth. So be strong and prove yourself a man.

kings1.2.p1.b3.text: And keep the charge of the LORD your God to walk in His ways … as is written in the Law of Moses

kings1.2.p1.b4.text: If your descendants take heed to walk faithfully before Me with all their heart and soul, you will never fail to have a man on the throne of Israel.

kings1.2.p2.b1.text: Moreover, you know what Joab son of Zeruiah did to me … He killed them in peacetime to avenge the blood of war.

kings1.2.p2.b2.text: But show loving devotion to the sons of Barzillai the Gileadite, and let them be among those who eat at your table

kings1.2.p2.b3.text: He called down bitter curses against me on the day I went to Mahanaim …

kings1.2.p2.b4.text: Now therefore, do not hold him guiltless, for you are a wise man. You know what you ought to do to him …

kings1.2.p3.b1.text: Then David rested with his fathers and was buried in the City of David.

kings1.2.p3.b2.text: The length of David’s reign over Israel was forty years—seven years in Hebron and thirty-three years in Jerusalem.

kings1.2.p3.b3.text: So Solomon sat on the throne of his father David, and his kingdom was firmly established.

kings1.2.p4.b2.text: You know that the kingship was mine … but the kingship has turned to my brother, for it has come to him from the LORD.

kings1.2.p4.b3.text: Please speak to King Solomon, since he will not turn you down. Let him give me Abishag the Shunammite as my wife.

kings1.2.p4.b4.text: Very well … I will speak to the king for you.

kings1.2.p5.b1.text: So Bathsheba went to King Solomon … The king stood up to greet her, bowed to her … who sat down at his right hand.

kings1.2.p5.b2.text: I have just one small request of you … Do not deny me.

kings1.2.p5.b3.text: Make your request, my mother … for I will not deny you.

kings1.2.p5.b4.text: Let Abishag the Shunammite be given to your brother Adonijah as his wife.

kings1.2.p6.b1.text: Why do you request Abishag the Shunammite for Adonijah? … you might as well request the kingdom for him

kings1.2.p6.b2.text: And now, as surely as the LORD lives … surely Adonijah shall be put to death today!

kings1.2.p6.b3.text: So King Solomon sent the order to Benaiah son of Jehoiada, who struck down Adonijah, and he died.

kings1.2.p7.b1.text: Go back to your fields in Anathoth. Even though you deserve to die,

kings1.2.p7.b2.text: I will not put you to death at this time, since you carried the ark of the Lord GOD before my father David, and you suffered through all that my father suffered.

kings1.2.p7.b3.text: So Solomon banished Abiathar from the priesthood of the LORD

kings1.2.p7.b4.text: and thus fulfilled the word that the LORD had spoken at Shiloh against the house of Eli.

kings1.2.p8.b1.text: When the news reached Joab … he fled to the tent of the LORD and took hold of the horns of the altar.

kings1.2.p8.b4.text: Do just as he says. Strike him down and bury him, and so remove from me and from the house of my father the innocent blood that Joab shed.

kings1.2.p8.b5.text: So Benaiah son of Jehoiada went up, struck down Joab, and killed him. He was buried at his own home in the wilderness.

kings1.2.p8.b6.text: And the king appointed Benaiah son of Jehoiada in Joab’s place over the army, and he appointed Zadok the priest in Abiathar’s place.

kings1.2.p9.b1.text: Build a house for yourself in Jerusalem and live there, but do not go anywhere else. On the day you go out and cross the Kidron Valley, know for sure that you will die

kings1.2.p9.b2.text: The sentence is fair … Your servant will do as my lord the king has spoken.

kings1.2.p9.b3.text: After three years, however, two of Shimei’s slaves ran away to Achish son of Maacah, king of Gath.

kings1.2.p9.b4.text: So Shimei saddled his donkey and set out to Achish at Gath in search of his slaves, and he brought them back from Gath.

kings1.2.p10.b1.text: Shimei had gone from Jerusalem to Gath and had returned,

kings1.2.p10.b2.text: So why have you not kept your oath to the LORD and the command that I gave you?”

kings1.2.p10.b3.text: You know in your heart all the evil that you did to my father David. Therefore the LORD will bring your evil back upon your head.

kings1.2.p10.b4.text: Then the king commanded Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and he went out and struck Shimei down, and he died.

kings1.2.p10.b5.text: Thus the kingdom was firmly established in the hand of Solomon.
